json.understood: Build a small web app that lets you add habits, tick them off each day, see your streaks, and keep the data in the browser's local storage.
json.title: Habit tracker app
json.objectWhy: A small app that does a job

steps.title: Build page
steps.does: Write index.html with the habit form, the habit list, the streak summary and the today heading as plain HTML.
steps.focus: Plain HTML only, no frameworks and no build step; every part that scripts will fill must already exist in the file as an empty element.

files.purpose: Page skeleton: header, add-habit form, habit list, streak summary, footer note about local storage

required.what: List of habits with tick buttons
Footer note that data stays in this browser

done: index.html opens on its own with no console errors
The form, list, streak summary, today heading and footer are all present in the HTML file itself

steps.title: Style app
steps.does: Write styles.css so the page is readable and each habit row, tick state and streak badge is clearly distinguishable.
steps.focus: Clean single-column layout, visible ticked versus unticked state, no image files: use CSS and inline SVG only.

files.purpose: Layout and look: form, habit rows, ticked state, streak badges

done: styles.css is linked from index.html and the page lays out without overlapping elements

steps.title: Wire storage
steps.does: Write app.js to add and remove habits, tick them off for a day, compute streaks, and save and load everything from local storage.
steps.focus: One local storage key holding all habits and their ticked dates; streaks counted in whole days; handle the empty state and a first visit with no saved data.

files.purpose: Habit add/remove, daily ticking, streak calculation, save and load from local storage

done: Adding a habit shows it in the list immediately
Ticking a day updates that habit's streak on screen
Reloading the page brings back the same habits and ticks
A second tick on the same day does not double-count

steps.title: Second read
steps.does: Read the finished files as a critical colleague and list what is weak, missing or confusing for a first-time user.
steps.focus: Whether streaks are explained, whether a wrong tick can be undone, and whether the saved data survives a page reload in the described way.
done: A short list of concrete weaknesses, each pointing at a file and a place in it

steps.title: Code check
steps.does: Check by code that the page parses, that styles.css and app.js are linked and resolve, and that the required parts are in index.html.
steps.focus: Broken paths, duplicate ids, required selectors missing from the HTML itself.
done: index.html parses and both linked files resolve
All required parts are found in index.html
Any failures are listed with the file and the reason

Skip to your habits

Your habits

    Nothing on the list yet. Add your first habit below and tick it today.

json.summary: Wrote index.html as a plain, semantic skeleton: viewport meta, styles.css linked and app.js loaded with defer, a skip link to the habit list, the today heading (#today), the habit list (ul#habit-list plus an empty-state note), the streak summary (#streak-summary with a short line explaining what a streak counts), the add-habit form (#habit-form with a labelled text field and an Add habit button), and a footer that says habits and ticks live in this browser's local storage. The elements that app.js will fill are present and empty, and there is no styling or behaviour in the file. Let me know if you want the add form placed above the habit list instead of below it. It will be shown to you for review, not saved yet.

plantedNotes: A script storage.js that the project doesn't have was linked (missing-file)
The link to #habit-list was changed to #habit-list-section, which the page doesn't have (broken-link)

json.summary: app.js adds and removes habits, toggles today's tick, computes streaks in whole days, renders the habit list and streak summary, and saves everything under one local storage key with empty and first-visit states handled.

plantedNotes: getElementById('today') was changed to look for "today-box" (element-missing)
A closing brace was removed from the script (parse-error)

json.summary: styles.css lays out the habit tracker as a single warm paper column: big tabular date, habit rows with a large tick box, green ticked state and clay streak badge, a quiet streak list, and a tinted add form, with a recomposed phone layout at 390 px and visible focus, hover and press states on every control.

json.verdict: The skeleton is solid and a normal reload does keep the habits, but the streak rule that zeroes the count before today's tick, the missing way to fix a wrong tick from an earlier day, and the silent wipe of an unreadable store are what a first-time user will actually trip on.

issues.text: The streak walks back from today and stops at the first gap, so a user who ticked yesterday but has not ticked yet this morning sees 0 days in every row badge and in the streak list. The single explaining line in index.html says a streak counts days in a row ending today, but never says the number falls to zero until you tick, which reads as a lost streak on day two.

Only today's tick can be undone. The tick button always adds or removes todayKey, and there is no view of earlier days and no edit at all, so a tick placed on the wrong day cannot be corrected from the app. The full history sits in habit.ticks but nothing in index.html ever shows it.

issues.about: app.js removeHabit, with styles.css @media (max-width: 34rem) habit-item grid
issues.text: Remove deletes the habit and every tick inside it straight away, with no confirmation and no undo; the only feedback is the screen reader announcement. In the 390 px layout the remove button shares the second grid row with the streak badge, one thumb-width from the tick box.

If the stored value is not valid JSON, readStore returns an empty list silently and storageWorks stays true, so the next save overwrites the key with only the new habits. The old data is destroyed with no message and no recovery path.

issues.about: index.html habit list section, with app.js renderEmptyNote
issues.text: The only text that says what a tick is, the empty note "Add your first habit below and tick it today", is hidden the moment one habit exists. After that the page shows an unlabelled square button per row, with nothing on screen saying that tapping ticks and tapping again unticks.

issues.about: index.html structure, with styles.css body background-image
issues.text: A habit tracker's own object is the grid of days being ticked, but the page shows only today, one square per habit. The grid appears only as decorative graph paper under the page, and no view shows yesterday or the last week, so a user can never see progress, only a number.

The aria-label stays "Tick <name> for today" when the habit is already ticked, so a screen reader announces a tick action on a ticked habit; it should flip to an untick wording with aria-pressed. The visible copy has the same gap, no row tells you the tick can be taken back.

checkDayChange calls render() with no focus spec, so at the day rollover (the 60 second interval, or coming back to the tab) every row is rebuilt and a keyboard user focused on a tick or remove button loses their place to the body.

unit.content:
Skip to your habits

Your habits

    Nothing on the list yet. Add your first habit below and tick it today.

    Current streaks

    A streak counts the days in a row that you ticked a habit, ending with today or yesterday.

    Add a habit

    Keep it small and repeatable, like reading ten pages or walking after lunch.

    Your habits, your ticks and your streaks are saved in this browser's local storage. Nothing is sent anywhere, and clearing site data removes them.

json.summary: styles.css now carries both themes through one set of tokens: the warm paper and ink green of the light theme, plus a dark block under html[data-theme="dark"] that app.js switches on and remembers in local storage. The masthead is a flex row so the day sits as the large element with the theme switch beside it, and the pill switch has hover, press and focus-visible states plus a tinted pressed state while the dark theme is on. Every other part stays as it was: habit rows with a large tick box whose check is invisible until the day is ticked, the green ticked row with its solid clay streak badge, the quiet streak list, the tinted add form, the skip link, notices and the 390 px phone layout where the switch moves to the top right and each row recomposes with the tick box beside the name.

json.verdict: The skeleton is solid and a normal reload does keep the habits, and the new theme switch does come back on the next visit, but the streak rule that zeroes the count before today's tick, the missing way to fix a wrong tick from an earlier day, the silent wipe of an unreadable store, and the wrong-theme flash the switch now introduces are what a first-time user will actually trip on.

issues.about: Streaks fall to zero until you tick, and the page never says so
issues.text: app.js streakEndingToday, with the explanation line p.streak-note in index.html: the streak walks back from today and stops at the first gap, so a user who ticked yesterday but has not ticked yet this morning sees 0 days in every row badge and in the streak list. The single explaining line in index.html says a streak counts the days in a row that you ticked, ending with today or yesterday, but the code only ever counts a run ending today, so that line is not even accurate. The number dropping to zero on day two reads as a lost streak.

issues.about: Only today's tick can be undone
issues.text: app.js toggleToday and buildRow: the tick button always adds or removes todayKey, and there is no view of earlier days and no edit at all, so a tick placed on the wrong day cannot be corrected from the app. The full history sits in habit.ticks but nothing in index.html ever shows it.

issues.about: The saved theme is applied too late, so a dark-theme user sees the light page first
issues.text: app.js start() and paintTheme(), with the dark block in styles.css under html[data-theme="dark"] and the deferred script tag in index.html. Nothing in the head sets the theme before the page paints: app.js is loaded with defer, reads the saved choice in start(), and only then writes data-theme on the html element. So on every load a user who chose dark sees the warm paper light theme, then the whole page flips. The same start() also builds the switch itself if index.html has no button in the masthead, so the control appears a moment after the day does. The footer in index.html says the habits, ticks and streaks are saved, but says nothing about the light or dark choice being remembered in this browser under its own key.

issues.about: An unreadable store is wiped without a word
issues.text: app.js readStore: if the stored value is not valid JSON, readStore returns an empty list silently and storageWorks stays true, so the next save overwrites the key with only the new habits. The old data is destroyed with no message and no recovery path for the user.

issues.about: Nothing on screen says what a tick does once a habit exists
issues.text: index.html habit-list section, with app.js renderEmptyNote: the only text that says what a tick is, the empty note in index.html reading "Add your first habit below and tick it today", is hidden the moment one habit exists. After that the page shows an unlabelled square button per row, with nothing visible saying that tapping ticks and tapping again unticks.

issues.about: The app's own object, the grid of days, is only decoration
issues.text: index.html structure, with the body background-image in styles.css: a habit tracker's own object is the grid of days being ticked, but the page shows only today, one square per habit. The grid appears only as decorative graph paper under the page, and no view shows yesterday or the last week, so a user can never see progress, only a number.

issues.about: Remove deletes the habit and its whole history at once
issues.text: app.js removeHabit, with the habit-item grid rules in styles.css under @media (max-width: 34rem): remove deletes the habit and every tick inside it straight away, with no confirmation and no undo; the only feedback is the screen reader announcement. In the 390 px layout the remove button shares the second grid row with the streak badge, one thumb-width from the tick box.

issues.about: Keyboard and screen reader state goes stale in each row
issues.text: app.js buildTickButton: the aria-label stays "Tick <name> for today" when the habit is already ticked, so a screen reader announces a tick action on a ticked habit; it should flip to an untick wording to match aria-pressed, and no visible copy tells you the tick can be taken back. app.js checkDayChange: it calls render() with no focus spec, so at the day rollover (the 60 second interval, or coming back to the tab) every row is rebuilt and a keyboard user focused on a tick or remove button loses their place to the body.
